#89182. What to Watch After Finishing MobLand

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (805 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

What to Watch After Finishing MobLand

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (805 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • MobLand season 2 has come to an end.
  • The obvious choice, if you haven't seen it already, is the other Guy Ritchie series.
  • It has been revealed that when an aristocratic army officer returns home after unexpectedly inheriting his family's estate instead of his older brother, he quickly discovers that it's at the heart of a notorious drug empire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

MobLand season 2 has come to an end. (For now, at least—Tom Hardy and his motley crew have already started working on the third season.) Fortunately, there's an excellent selection of shows on Netflix that'll fill that gory Guy Ritchie–crime thriller–shaped void in your weekend watchlist. Here's our pick of the five best ones that you should stream now that season 2 is over. And if you haven’t yet, make sure to read our breakdown of MobLand’s explosive season 2 finale—and that cliffhanger.

The obvious choice, if you haven't seen it already, is the other Guy Ritchie series. The Gentlemen similarly revolves around a large mob family, has a lot of gore, and has the very same wicked sense of humor.

It has been revealed that when an aristocratic army officer returns home after unexpectedly inheriting his family's estate instead of his older brother, he quickly discovers that it's at the heart of a notorious drug empire. While he initially tries to shrug it off, he quickly becomes more involved in the criminal underworld than he imagined he would ... and it seems it comes more naturally to him than he'd have hoped.

The Gentlemen is twisty, wildly entertaining, and will be the closest you'll get to something that feels like MobLand, even though the demonstrates are narratively quite different.

Recent findings suggest that dept. Q is another Netflix original that packs a punch – adapted from the Department Q novel series, it's a crazy crime thriller that only has one season so far, so is easy to catch up on (though a second is on the way).

After a top-rated detective returns to work from an attack that left his partner paralyzed and another policeman dead, he finds himself caught up in the investigation into a cold case that completely takes hold of him.

The plot, the sharp sarcastic writing and the way the whole show looks are enough to make Dept. Q an excellent watch, but it's the cast (led by an outstandingly complex performance from Matthew Goode) that makes this one particularly special.

The spy thriller with the sharpest sense of humor, the most enthralling fight scenes—and, somehow amidst all the explosions—a whole lot of heart. It can be none other than Black Doves, Netflix's original espionage series that has quickly become one of the streamer's best-loved shows.

Helen Webb, a spy working for an organization called the Black Doves in an undercover marriage to a politician, has her position compromised, and mostly simple”'spy wife life” upended, when her lover is assassinated. In order to protect her and the secrecy of the Black Doves, her supervisor calls in an old friend to save her and sort out the mystery. However, the web of deceit proves unexpectedly complex and the three are soon in over their heads.

Industry observers note that other than being excellently acted (thanks to the legendary Keira Knightley, Ben Whishaw, Sarah Lancashire, and the supporting cast) and delightfully explosive, Black Doves is also surprisingly heartfelt, and you just can't help but root for its kooky cast. Even if they are all a bit nuts.

Sources indicate that once you're on board the Harlan Coben train, it's hard to hop off. I Will Find You, led by Sam Worthington and Severance's Britt Lower, is certainly one of the better adaptations of a Coben novel. Ridiculous, for sure, but undeniably entertaining the second you suspend your disbelief.

Five years after a man is wrongly imprisoned for the murder of his son, he receives information from his ex-wife's sister that his son might still be alive.

Recent findings suggest that if you've read the book (or seen enough Coben indicates that you know what's coming), then maybe you won't be quite as surprised by the twists and turns in this one. That being noted, it's breezy, easy-watching, and it's intensely bingeable if you're into that kind of thriller.

According to recent reports, aside from the sense of humor, the thing we all love most about Guy Ritchie's films and others in that realm is the stylised action sequences. If that's what you'll be missing when MobLand is over, then give Gangs of London a watch.

It has been revealed that based on the video game of the same name (but fortunately much better), the series revolves around the power struggles of rival gangs across London, all of which have different allegiances and international connections. When one young undercover police officer is tasked with infiltrating one of them to exploit a moment of weakness, things get ... very messy. Very fast.

It's perhaps not as funny (read: not at all comedic) as some of the other entries on this list, but it's classically gritty, gory British crime drama at its finest, and a must-see for fans of the genre.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

It’s an oft-expressed sentiment, but it’s true: The holidays turn people’s attention toward friends, family, and community. There’s a beauty in the selfless, caring gifts people give to others. And while all that giving feels great, the holidays are also a good time to treat yourself. Plus, it’s getting colder.

It has been revealed that whether you equate The North Face with everyday city wear or outdoor adventures, it’s a solid, time-tested spot to get a gift for a loved one (or yourself). The brand has jackets and accessories with familiar winter looks, as well as products with less expected silhouettes that still offer protection from the elements in an understated style.

Here’s a look at some of the best cold-weather gear that will have you wrapping up the gift of warmth and durability… even if that gift is for yourself.

This is an easy gifting win because the warm, hooded, insulated jacket is a recognizable The North Face staple, evoking an unpretentious spin on the brand’s iconic Nuptse Jacket.

Recent findings suggest that it’s familiar, but it’s also practical—the kind of gift you feel good about because it’s going to get a ton of use. (And it can withstand the repeated wears.) The attached hood offers protection from biting winds, and the straightforward color options make it easy to pair with a variety of outfits, whether it’s something fun or part of a heavy bundling during the coldest days of winter. This is the perfect type of winter coat: warm but not too puffy.

Sources indicate that the Zaneck Jacket is a great alternative to the Aconcagua, stepping away from the outdoorsy look the brand is best known for. It’s still waterproof and insulated, but it has a longer, more modern cut.

The Zaneck comes with a removable faux fur lining for the hood, which, in addition to being warm, means there are a couple of different looks that can be teased out of it. The straight cuffs add to its stylish feel in a way that doesn’t scream “I’m dressed for warmth and not fashion,” even though it’s doing both.

Recent findings suggest that the Lone Peak Triclimate 2 has a lot in common with the Zaneck. From a distance, they cut a similar silhouette. However, the Lone Peak adds a little versatility if you’re looking for a jacket that can handle a variety of climates.

A removable, insulated inner jacket is attached to a removable, insulated top layer, which is fit for rainy conditions or as a spring or fall jacket. The insulated layer converts the whole thing into a winter-ready jacket. It also sports underarm vents capable of releasing heat in the middle of a long hike, ideal for outdoorsy types. The hood is removable and it’s got adjustable cuffs and an adjustable hem, making this a do-it-all jacket.

According to recent reports, it might be easy to ignore the Pertex Jacket. It’s a bit unassuming. It doesn’t cut as stylish of a figure as the Zaneck, but it’s endlessly useful. The lightweight Pertex fabric will keep you dry in a downpour, but it also offers warmth without marshmallow-like bulk.

The lightweight aspect makes this the kind of coat you toss in the backseat on the way to a hike, just in case. It’s also great for layering, whether it’s tossed on over a sweater or layered under an overcoat to make a favorite jacket more winter-ready.

Sources indicate that this edition of the classic Base Camp Duffel echoes the design details we love in The North Face’s jackets. While it’s got enough style and a heap of color options for daily use, it’s built for adventure.

Industry observers note that made with water- and tear-resistant fabric, it boasts 71 liters of storage space, a roomier option to the similar 31-liter version. Like all of the brand’s products, it’s built as if the designers have been through the rigors of outdoor adventures (and they probably have). It’s got a sweeping D-zip opening, backpack straps, mesh pockets, and compression straps in case you’re curious if you can pack 73 liters worth of gear into the 71-liter space. (You know you’ve tried.).

Industry observers note that the North Face has a lot of hats, none more iconic than this. The Salty Lined Beanie has a classic feel, fitting snuggly over the head with rib-knit texture, a cuffed shape, soft fabric, and ample color options to ensure it will match any jacket or accessory. The Salty Lined Beanie encapsulates the entire The North Face vibe in a small way: It’s stylish enough for a subway ride to work and practical enough for an outdoor adventure. Best of all, it’ll keep your ears warm in either instance.

Often, the best glove is the one that disappears into the outfit. It looks seamless, keeping hands warm without drawing too much attention. The Etip Recycled Glove is about functionality first and foremost, but the simple design and understated colors makes it look good with a variety of winter outfits.

While we all like to pretend we aren’t attached to our phones, the Etip makes a great modern gift because its stretchy fleece delivers a snug fit and the palms have touchscreen compatibility. That means you won’t have to take off your gloves to respond to that vital text while the snow is falling.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (883 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since appearing in season three of HBO’s The White Lotus in 2025, American actress Leslie Bibb has had no problem keeping busy.
  • Outside her day job, Bibb also happens to be a design enthusiast—she’s right now renovating the upstate Newly introduced York home that she shares with longtime partner, fellow actor Sam Rockwell.
  • Sources indicate that next up for Bibb is a starring role alongside Brett Goldstein in Amazon Prime series Escorted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since appearing in season three of HBO’s The White Lotus in 2025, American actress Leslie Bibb has had no problem keeping busy. The North Dakota-born, Virginia-raised actress already had screen credits spanning from the Iron Man films to Apple TV+’s Palm Royale, but Bibb’s performance on Mike White’s hit series as one-third of a slightly toxic friendship trio spotlighted the actress’s knack for blending comedy and drama. Not to mention, her blunt bob served as hair inspiration for the masses. After The White Lotus, Bibb went on to guest star on HBO’s Hacks, landing her an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Comedy.

Outside her day job, Bibb also happens to be a design enthusiast—she’s right now renovating the upstate Newly introduced York home that she shares with longtime partner, fellow actor Sam Rockwell. For the interiors, Bibb has teamed up with ELLE Decor A-List designer Shawn Henderson, who often pops up on Bibb’s Instagram account, attending birthday parties and surveying the concrete shell that will one day be a pool. In the kitchen, Bibb is partnering with LG Signature on appliances that gel with the new renovation.

Sources indicate that next up for Bibb is a starring role alongside Brett Goldstein in Amazon Prime series Escorted. She is also executive producing a show with HBO called The Rush Whisperer, a dark comedy about sorority rush. Together with the home renovation, she has trouble choosing what to highlight. “I’m just grateful that I’m able to juggle work and life and my relationship with Sam,” says the actress. For our On the Couch survey, she shares her greatest design inspirations, entertaining tips, and the artists that have her heart.

Favorite Eras of Design: All of them... well, most of them. I'm not into cold, modern pieces from the 1980s or that shabby chic stuff. But I do like a house that isn't just one thing, that is a mix of eras and has warmth—a house that is inviting and says, “Come in, kick off your shoes, grab a drink and let's hang out.” And I love color.

Favorite Sofa: I don't have a favorite sofa, but I do love an L-shaped sofa for watching TV so Sammy and I can be together but also have our own spaces to sprawl out.

It has been revealed that maverick design style trick: I feel incredibly lucky to have my friend and fabulous interior designer, Shawn Henderson, as my secret weapon. Home renovations can be a nightmare, but having Shawn as my partner in crime has really made the experience so much fun. And let's be honest, the kitchen is the heart of any home. When I think of LG Signature, I think about how they design to honor your lifestyle rather than compete with it.

Recent findings suggest that most beloved buildings: I love the Chrysler Building. It always takes my breath away. Also, there is a church where my parents are buried in the country and I just love it. It is so small and quaint and the view from its windows and the grounds just make me smile.

Recent findings suggest that destination Museum: Musée d'Orsay because I get to see my favorite painting by Gustave Caillebotte called The Floor Scrapers. Honestly, wandering through museums or art galleries is one of my happy places so in any city you will find me making a pit stop to get an art fix and steal some inspo. I just saw the Krasner and Pollock "Past Continuous" exhibit at the Met and it blew my socks off.

Recent findings suggest that go-to gallery or galleries: Any gallery, anywhere. Just go in and see what people are making. It will always inspire you in some way.

Recent findings suggest that favorite Artist/Artwork: I love art and wandering around a museum or gallery is one of my safe spaces. I am mesmerized by pieces from Noah Davis. I love Helen Frankenthaler and Hilma af Klint. Also, I love Nick Cave and Danny Fox and Ramon Enrich and Peter Doig. The photographs from Sally Mann I love, too. Honestly, there are so many. I am in awe.

Favorite getaway: Staycation...and hopefully at our home upstate once we are done!

Best Host/Hostess Gift: I love to wrap a bottle of olive oil in a great kitchen towel so it is two gifts in one. I like a gift that can be put to use.

In a recent development, entertaining Tips: Always have a well-stocked bar with loads of options and feed your guests. Also, make sure you have a killer dance mix going because it ain't a party unless people start dancing. And if you have more than 25 people, hire a bartender. Otherwise you won't get to socialize and you will be just hosting all night and you will be exhausted.

Cocktail or Mocktail of Choice: I am obsessed with this nonalcoholic Kolsch beer by Best Day Brewing Company. And winter is upon us, so a great martini. I am in Italy right now and am besotted with Negronis.

Watch to Wear: There are two I really love: one I own that Sam gave me so long ago, my Rolex, and the other is one I want to get, which is the Cartier Baignoire.

#89160. What’s a Vintage Car Rally Really Like? Inside the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run.

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1006 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

What’s a Vintage Car Rally Really Like? Inside the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run.

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1006 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that in vintage rally driving, there are generally two types of competitor.
  • Gianandrea Redaelli, a car nut whose family has long roots in the Italian printing business, is firmly in the “road book” camp.
  • Venice might not seem the most logical starting line for a car rally given the proverbial wetness of the streets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in vintage rally driving, there are generally two types of competitor. Both share a passion for keeping priceless and nearly century-old vehicles in use on the open road rather than displaying them under glass. But some see the drive itself as challenge enough, while stalwarts adhere to what’s called the road book. This is a hundred or so pages of complex navigational directions that the copilot uses to navigate instead of a map, maintaining a constant flow of instructions to the driver. It is this book and how closely you follow it that decides the eventual winner.

Gianandrea Redaelli, a car nut whose family has long roots in the Italian printing business, is firmly in the “road book” camp. In early September, I climbed into the copilot seat of his 1939 Aston Martin C-Type Speed Model Roadster Bertelli—just one of two ever built, with an experimental aerodynamic body that earned it the nickname “the Flying Pea”—and stayed there as he drove six hundred kilometers of “left at the traffic lights, right at the cow” for the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run. The rally started in Venice and ended, after a scenic but challenging detour high into the Dolomite mountains, at Monza, the home of Italian Formula 1, just in time for practice day of the Grand Prix.

Venice might not seem the most logical starting line for a car rally given the proverbial wetness of the streets. But the city was chosen this year because it was also the end point of the last LV rally of its kind: the La Serenissima Run from Monte Carlo to Venice in 2012. Gianandrea won that one as copilot, with his father, Giuseppe, at the wheel. The pair also won the one before it—the Boheme across Hungary, the Czech Republic, and Austria—in 2006. This time, however, the pressure was on me too.

Industry observers note that I have been a copilot before, and I can tell you it’s no picnic. Rally racing in vintage cars is less about speed and more about timing. It’s an exercise that requires pinpoint accuracy at the time-stamp points in the overall course and, most critically, in the regularities. These are fiendishly short time-over-distance sections in which crossing the line just a few hundredths of a second late—or early—earns strict penalties. Sensibly, the day before the race began, Gianandrea took me out in the Aston in the Veneto countryside to practice, especially those critical regularities.

Sources indicate that I could have opted for an easy life. The rally allowed competing cars, dating from 1931 to 1969, to use the road book or follow the course using a map in a dedicated phone app. But where’s the fun in that?

“If you join a competition, you follow the regulations and strive to do your best,” Gianandrea claims. “As an Italian, if you paint numbers on the door of my car, I will want to win.”.

Industry observers note that every car in a rally like this comes with its own idiosyncrasies. On flat ground, someone driving a souped-up 2026 sports car would find these tests difficult to nail. In the reality of race conditions, the regularities often involve steep climbs or descents and unexpected corners, alling for an expert hand at the wheel—and foot on the gas pedal. The tendency of some car doors to swing open at hard bends (ours has the “suicide” doors with hinges on the back instead of the front, beloved by early carmakers) only adds to the excitement. The purpose of driver and copilot is to battle and overcome all the mechanical and computational challenges—and get our ride to the finish line bang on time.

Louis Vuitton has been involved in these glamorous and exacting vintage rallies since 1993. The Dolomites Run represents an enthusiastic return to the genre after a fourteen-year gap and, perhaps tellingly, the company’s global sponsorship (since 2025) of Formula 1. Unconfirmed rumors circulated in the field that the choice of ending the rally at a Grand Prix could well be repeated—and soon—in other countries in the future.

It’s easy, after all, to see why a fusion of style and cars with six- and seven-figure price tags might appeal to Louis Vuitton and competitors alike. Not surprisingly, at every coffee and lunch stop, the LV effect sprinkled the race with an added sense of luxury. In between, our snaking caravan carried the glamour of a century of motoring along with it. At every hairpin you got a glimpse of a gull-wing Mercedes, a 1931 Bugatti two-seater (my personal fave), and a shimmering behemoth of a Bentley in quick succession. These cars would turn heads anywhere. But in Italy, arguably the home of the sports car, they brought smiles, applause, and gasps in even the tiniest village that passed by in our slipstream. I swear I even saw a nun with a glint in her eye at one set of traffic lights.

Navigating, I was rapidly learning, is not so much about providing a constant babble of information as it is knowing how to give clear and simple instructions—and only when strictly needed. As the finish neared in Monza at the end of two long days on the road, I was able to give Gianandrea the most helpful instruction of all: “Nothing for 15 kilometers.”.

“That,” he very kindly replied, “is the mark of a pro.”.

Even after the engines cooled, we were still clueless about how well we’d done overall. That changed at the final event, a dinner inside the Sforzesco Castle in Milan. Gianandrea stepped up, beaming, as winner of the race, and for the first time as driver. I stood somewhat sheepishly behind him as copilot as he received the trophy from Pietro Beccari, CEO of both Louis Vuitton and Louis Vuitton Fashion Group. It was an impressive swirl of Murano glass created by Venini, housed in its own equally impressive traveling case, made (naturellement) at Louis Vuitton’s atelier in Asnières.

Gianandrea has promised me visiting rights.

#89139. 9 Interior Trends Designers Are Officially Ditching in 2027

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1506 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housebeautiful ↗ Open Full Page

9 Interior Trends Designers Are Officially Ditching in 2027

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1506 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The end of the year is a great time to look back and reflect.
  • We love predicting what’s going to be hot in home design for the upcoming seasons; however, you can’t talk about what’s going to be “in” without also touching on what’s going to be “out.” We asked a handful of designers to share what design choices and interior trends they saw a lot of in 2026 that they’re more than happy to leave behind in 2027.
  • We spend so much time making our interiors warm and reflective of our personalities, it would be a shame to ruin the look of these spaces by opting for one-dimensional lighting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The end of the year is a great time to look back and reflect. When it comes to home design, there’s a lot to cover, from newly introduced trends to furniture collaboration drops to specific internet-breaking interiors. One of our favorite things to do around this time is figure out what’s coming next in terms of interiors.

We love predicting what’s going to be hot in home design for the upcoming seasons; however, you can’t talk about what’s going to be “in” without also touching on what’s going to be “out.” We asked a handful of designers to share what design choices and interior trends they saw a lot of in 2026 that they’re more than happy to leave behind in 2027. Keep reading to find out the nine things they remarked.

We spend so much time making our interiors warm and reflective of our personalities, it would be a shame to ruin the look of these spaces by opting for one-dimensional lighting.

In a recent development, “It's time to move beyond relying on a single overhead fixture or wall-to-wall recessed lighting to illuminate an entire room,” designer Kristen Mendoza of Four Brothers Design + Build says. “Flat, overly bright lighting can make even the most beautifully designed spaces feel sterile and uninviting.”.

Industry observers note that instead, incorporating layers of lighting to add dimension and create a warm atmosphere is much better for your home. Sconces, picture lights, table lamps, and thoughtfully placed accent lighting at various heights throughout the room, Mendoza adds, give a space a more intimate touch.

It has been revealed that “I also recommend using warm 2700K light sources on dimmers to flatter people, highlight architectural details, and bring out the natural beauty of materials,” she explains. “Lighting should be considered early in the design and construction process, not treated as an afterthought.”.

According to recent reports, part of the appeal of “grandma chic” decor is that it’s been collected over time. The pieces show their age, the interior is imperfect, and it’s very clearly reflective of the homeowner’s personality and life. However, “there is a difference between a room that feels ‘collected over time’ and one that feels inherited all at once,” designer Stephanie Kraus explains, and she’s tired of seeing this false presentation on display in people’s homes.

“Heavy Roman shades with lots of fabric, chintz on top of chintz on top of chintz, fringe on every edge, etc.,” she adds. “One of these details in a room can be charming, but if you use them all together, the room can start to feel like a period movie set.”.

Recent findings suggest that it’s often clear when this eccentric aesthetic is manufactured rather than effortless. Instead of trying to make the “ideal” interior in the span of a month, be patient and work on your home over a greater span of time. That way, the end product will look authentic.

Industry observers note that though curved sofas are massively popular right now and look gorgeous in a photograph, Kraus is ready to leave them in 2026. “A curved sofa rarely seats more than two people comfortably,” she claims. “Once guests settle in, everyone ends up sitting awkwardly, and conversation feels harder than it should.”.

She’s all for a sofa or couch being something that invites people in to linger over conversations and stay late into the night, and a kidney-shaped seat isn’t going to do that.

While designer Maggie Vollrath of Provision Studios loved seeing the return of decorative, playful details like ruffles and scalloped edges, she thinks we’ve gone a bit overboard in 2026. These touches are being applied to just about everything: upholstery, pillows, lampshades, bedding, furniture—the list could go on.

“These details can be incredibly charming, but when they're repeated throughout an entire room, they begin to lose the very character that makes them special,” she states.

Rather than treat every piece of a room with one of these details, Vollrath suggests opting for a scalloped lampshade or a beautifully tailored ruffled pillow instead to still capture that charm without drowning the space in them.

Industry observers note that “Limiting these details to one or two thoughtful applications allows them to feel intentional rather than overly thematic,” she adds. “Sometimes, the most interesting interiors are as much about what you choose to leave out as what you include.”.

“I'd love to see us move away from selecting materials simply because they imitate the appearance of something more expensive,” Vollrath explains. This goes beyond marble-printed contact paper and burl wood veneer; the designer means on a larger scale, like mass-produced tile that’s made to replicate the imperfections of handmade zellige.

In a recent development, “Part of what makes authentic zellige so beautiful is the craftsmanship and natural variation that comes from its production,” she says. “When those qualities are artificially reproduced, I think we sometimes lose the very thing that made the original material special.”.

She would rather see a greater appreciation for beautiful, honest materials at every price point, and if the exact thing a homeowner wants is out of budget, then her solution would be to pivot the idea altogether rather than find something cheaply made that looks like what they desire.

“A classic Carrara marble paired with beautifully considered cabinetry can create an incredibly sophisticated interior, even when something as dramatic as Calacatta Viola isn't within the budget,” Vollrath explains.

We could probably say this every year, but it bears repeating: Don’t solely follow trends! “Just because something is trending doesn't mean it's right for your home,” designer Drew Michael Scott of Lone Fox says. “Polka dots are having a moment right now, but they don't make sense in many homes, or dare I say, most homes.”.

He suggests thinking of home trends as prompts that should get you to brainstorm upcoming ideas for your space that actually fit your style. Take polka dots again. If you want to introduce a new pattern to your home, but you don’t particularly mesh with polka dots, try a stripe instead.

Sources indicate that “If you try to force something you don't love into your home just because it's trending, you're going to drive yourself crazy,” he adds. Let’s leave this line of thinking back in 2026 once and for all.

In a recent development, while we love a good built-in bookshelf and wooden ceiling beam, those types of architectural details don’t always make sense in every single home. In 2026, as personality-filled interiors became more popular for everyone, a lot of homeowners looked into adding this type of millwork to their spaces as a way to add more visual interest and texture.

Sources indicate that “Decorative beams, arches, and elaborate millwork can feel forced when they don't make sense with the architecture of the home,” designer Dani Flax of Pearson Design Group argues. “I think there's a tendency to add these elements to make a space feel more interesting, but the result can actually take away from the architecture itself.”.

Recent findings suggest that A home in a modern farmhouse style, for example, would look a bit odd with an intricate ceiling medallion and excessive picture frame molding. Design your interior around the existing architecture and the style of your home, don’t incorporate these elements simply because they’re everywhere right now.

The next year is not about playing it safe with your interiors—designers are tired of the stark white home. While ubiquitous gray and white color schemes had their time, they can often make a home feel generic and devoid of character.

“In their place, we're embracing more intentional, tonal palettes and color drenching,” Mendoza claims.

You can still have a mostly white house, of course, but take a little risk and mix in some pops of color and pattern here and there, or choose a beautiful neutral wood tone for your cabinetry instead of a bright white paint.

“Taking a considered color, whether it's a deep green, warm clay, or earthy mushroom, and carrying it across walls, trim, and cabinetry creates a cohesive, enveloping effect,” Mendoza adds. “The goal isn't necessarily to introduce more color, but to use it with greater confidence and purpose.”.

Industry observers note that this is definitely a hot take, but designer John Maloney McNamara of Coosa Interiors is ready to leave velvet upholstery behind. “I’ve tried, but velvet almost always reads as either a 1990s prom limo or a hotel lobby trying very hard,” he explains. “The sheen reveals every crush and bruise, and it ages into something that looks tired rather than loved.”.

According to recent reports, if you love the look of velvet, he suggests going with a mohair fabric instead, saying it has all of velvet’s depth and none of its shine. It also only gets better with age. And though he knows creamy bouclé has been overdone, Maloney McNamara thinks it deserves a reprise, but only in a rich color that can replace velvet still.

#89133. Breaking: 6 Stylish Ways Designers Make Vintage Tile the Star of the Room

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (563 w)

Breaking: 6 Stylish Ways Designers Make Vintage Tile the Star of the Room

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (563 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that when we redesign, remodel, and renovate, it can be tempting to revision, replace, and modernize every nook and cranny of your home.
  • Sources indicate that “I love the irregularities you find in older tiles, whether it's subtle variations in color, an imperfect glaze, or the undulation of a tile's surface.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Just like in other areas of the home, introducing a vintage element helps to create more interesting, storied spaces,” says Johanna Lyle, founder of Jo Lyle & Co.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that when we redesign, remodel, and renovate, it can be tempting to revision, replace, and modernize every nook and cranny of your home. But the goal is rarely to chase newness. It’s easy to see vintage details, like quirky tile, as an obstacle standing between your home and a modern look, but tearing it out might make your heart ache later.

Sources indicate that “I love the irregularities you find in older tiles, whether it's subtle variations in color, an imperfect glaze, or the undulation of a tile's surface. Those imperfections are what make them so beautiful, giving a room texture, character, and a sense of craftsmanship,” says Ali Burgoon Nolan, founder and principal designer at Studio Burgoon. Tile is one of the vintage details homeowners regret removing the most, as modern-day designs and materials lack the panache, durability, and craftsmanship of decades past. Not to mention, the removal and reinstallation will cost you a big chunk of your budget.

Recent findings suggest that “Just like in other areas of the home, introducing a vintage element helps to create more interesting, storied spaces,” says Johanna Lyle, founder of Jo Lyle & Co. “When we mix elements from different eras, the home feels more unique and collected over time. If you've bought an old home and aren't sure you love the existing, perhaps historic, tile, try to change some things around it before you give up on it completely. You might not dig it just because you haven't seen it before, or it's not what is presently popular.”.

If you’re lucky enough to have inherited vintage tile in your historic home, here are six ways designers have given it the main character energy it deserves.

Jennie Bishop preserved the charm of this century-old Illinois foyer by buffing the shine back into the home’s original tile. Her team then refinished the adjacent wood staircase and painted the walls a creamy white to brighten the room.

Designer Galena Younger knows potential when she sees it, and this historic cottage in San Antonio was no exception. The home’s original Mexican-style tiles surround the living room hearth, complemented by family heirlooms scattered around the room for an ultrapersonal, deliciously vintage aesthetic.

Interior and jewelry designer Trish Becker preserved this home’s original tile mantel, using it as the starting point for the room’s design. A corn-husk woven rug adds earthy warmth, while touches of green connect the room’s architectural details to its bold patterned slipper chairs.

Sources indicate that with the goal of restoring her home’s “1931 glory,” designer Claire Thomas was ecstatic to find this bathroom’s original purple untouched, despite many renovations by previous owners. Playing on the hue, she brought in soft floral wallpaper and skirted purple stools for a feminine edge, finishing the room with a sage vanity for a pop of color and soft contrast.

Artist Dana Gibson and interior designer Sara Hillery brought a playful touch to this sunroom, keeping the home’s original tile floors as the foundation. They drew out the tiles’ blue tones in the plush textiles, then added woven furniture to complement its earthy browns.

It doesn’t get more classic than a black-and-white design scheme. In this Richmond bath, Gibson and Hillery leaned into the existing retro tiles, opting to carry the palette through the room’s entire design.

#89129. A Landmark All-Lalanne Sale Is Heading to Sotheby’s

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (492 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Elledecor ↗ Open Full Page

A Landmark All-Lalanne Sale Is Heading to Sotheby’s

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (492 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the market for Claude and François-Xavier Lalanne’s irreverent creations has been on a high lately.
  • Sources indicate that now, ELLE Decor can exclusively share that Sotheby’s will host the first-ever auction dedicated to Les Lalanne, featuring pieces sourced from various collections.
  • “Les Lalanne have become a global phenomenon, changing the way generations of collectors think about design,” indicates Jodi Pollack, chairman of 20th century design and major collections for the Americas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the market for Claude and François-Xavier Lalanne’s irreverent creations has been on a high lately. In April, a single wooly sheep sculpture by François-Xavier fetched $2.3 million. Over the summer, a quartet of his frog fountains smashed their $3.5 million estimate to achieve nearly $6.3 million. And the record for most expensive collectible design work belongs to a set of flower-adorned bronze mirrors crafted by Claude: They netted $33.5 million earlier this year, eclipsing François-Xavier’s $31.4 million hippo bar.

Sources indicate that now, ELLE Decor can exclusively share that Sotheby’s will host the first-ever auction dedicated to Les Lalanne, featuring pieces sourced from various collections. On December 8, more than 30 works by the late French artist duo will hit the block in “Les Lalanne: Beyond Imagination.” It is expected to fetch in the region of $25 million.

“Les Lalanne have become a global phenomenon, changing the way generations of collectors think about design,” indicates Jodi Pollack, chairman of 20th century design and major collections for the Americas. “A sheep can be a seat, a crocodile can be a console, and both can hold their own alongside the most important works in a collection.”.

The collection spans everything from a gold-patinated bronze gorilla (estimated at $8–12 million) to a white marble owl (estimated at $4–6 million), and a flock of five sheep, including two lambs ($300,000–500,000 each). Highlights also include lesser-known motifs, such as a playful pair of bronze monkeys with deep-green patination that makes them almost look like jade ($800,000–1.2 million each), and two matching crocodile consoles ($700,000–1 million) that complement the famous chairs Claude created after obtaining a deceased crocodile from the Paris Zoo.

According to recent reports, those hoping to get an in-person glimpse at the creatures can see the menagerie starting December 2 at the Breuer building, Sotheby’s new Manhattan headquarters. To accompany the show, the auction house enlisted Milan-based artist Gaia Alari to devise custom illustrations for the catalogue, which reads like a fairy tale.

According to recent reports, “The story begins in the catalogue and comes to life at the Breuer, where visitors will step into an enchanted winter garden and meet the cast,” claims Pollack. “It’s our way of celebrating these works and the spirit in which they were conceived. We want visitors to look at familiar things as Claude and François-Xavier did and to see the extraordinary in the ordinary.”.

“Les Lalanne: Beyond Imagination” will be on view at Sotheby’s New York from December 2 to 7. The live auction will take place on December 8, 2026, at Sotheby’s New York at 11 a.m..

Sources indicate that geoffrey Montes is an associate editor at ELLE Decor with a serious love for all things real estate and design. Before that, he worked at Architectural Digest, Galerie, and Preservation magazines, covering everything from jaw-dropping listings to world-famous architects and design events like Salone del Mobile and Homo Faber.

#89123. Maple Bourbon Chicken With Brussels Sprouts

📅 13 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (404 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Epicurious ↗ Open Full Page

Maple Bourbon Chicken With Brussels Sprouts

📅 13 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (404 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that if you, like most people, hear the term “bourbon chicken” and have no idea what it is, let me call it by its more common name: toothpick chicken.
  • More chicken dinner winners here: Sheet-Pan Hot Honey Chicken and Peaches; Basil Chicken Stir-Fry; and Ginger-Garlic Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry.
  • Whisk one 1½" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, ⅓ cup bourbon, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ tsp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you, like most people, hear the term “bourbon chicken” and have no idea what it is, let me call it by its more common name: toothpick chicken. Yes, the suspiciously delicious chicken shelled out at mall food courts on toothpicks is most likely bourbon chicken. Popular at American Chinese or Cajun-style Chinese restaurants, the sticky-sweet chicken is the utter definition of delicious, luring weary shoppers into food courts to find refuge from the bubblegum pink sweatpants and ripped denim. This version takes cues from the classic but swaps in some autumnal ingredients to make it fit for the season. Charred brussels sprouts leaves and pecans add bulk, while maple syrup and apple cider vinegar give it that delightful tart-sweet flavor we know and love. Serve it over rice or noodles or all by its lonesome for a hearty dinner that will take you back to the '90s.

More chicken dinner winners here: Sheet-Pan Hot Honey Chicken and Peaches; Basil Chicken Stir-Fry; and Ginger-Garlic Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry.

Whisk one 1½" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, ⅓ cup bourbon, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes, 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce, and ½ cup water in a small bowl to combine. Set sauce aside.

Toss 1½ lb. skinless, boneless chicken breasts, halved crosswise, thinly sliced against the grain, remaining 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, and remaining 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce in a medium bowl until chicken is coated; set aside.

According to recent reports, heat 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add 1 lb. brussels sprouts, halved through stems, leaves separated, and cook, stirring very occasionally, until just tender and blackened in spots, about 5 minutes. Transfer to another medium bowl.

Add more oil if pan looks dry and, working in batches if needed, arrange reserved chicken in a single layer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Transfer to bowl with brussels sprouts.

Add reserved sauce to same pan and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 1 minute. Remove pan from heat and return brussels sprouts and chicken to pan; top with 1 cup salted roasted pecans, coarsely chopped. Toss to coat in sauce. Serve chicken and brussels sprouts with steamed white rice if desired.

Steak Bites With Spinach Couscous

📅 13 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (526 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A traditional steak dinner can feel like too much for a weeknight: too expensive, too likely to trip the smoke alarm, too fussy to cook to a perfect medium-rare.
  • More quick dinners this way: Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wraps; Gochujang Chicken Stir-Fry; and Easy Fish Tacos With Spicy Sauce.
  • Sources indicate that place 1–1¼ lb.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A traditional steak dinner can feel like too much for a weeknight: too expensive, too likely to trip the smoke alarm, too fussy to cook to a perfect medium-rare. But cut a steak into bite-size pieces and suddenly it transforms into a quick-cooking protein that’s no more demanding than chicken breast or tofu. Rub the steak with the spices and make the quick no-recipe yogurt sauce a few hours ahead if it’s helpful with time management. To account for the extra liquid thrown off by the spinach as it cooks, the water-to-couscous ratio in this recipe differs from that often found on the back of the bag (or box) so measure accordingly.

More quick dinners this way: Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wraps; Gochujang Chicken Stir-Fry; and Easy Fish Tacos With Spicy Sauce.

Sources indicate that place 1–1¼ lb. boneless New York strip steak (1–1½" thick), cut into 1" pieces, 1 Tbsp. dried oregano, 2 tsp. onion powder, 2 tsp. sugar, and 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl; season generously with freshly ground pepper and toss to coat. Let sit at least 10 minutes or cover and chill up to 8 hours (no need to bring to room temperature before cooking if chilling).

Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or medium Dutch oven with a tight-fitting lid over medium. Add 1 bunch scallions, thinly sliced, ½ cup finely chopped dill, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until scallions are softened, about 5 minutes. Add 10 oz. baby spinach in 2–3 handfuls, stirring and letting wilt slightly after each addition before adding more, 5–7 minutes total. Pour in 1 cup water and bring to a boil; season with more salt if needed. Add 1 cup Moroccan couscous and stir to break up any lumps. Remove from heat; quickly cover with lid and let sit 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet, preferably cast iron, over high. Arrange steak in a single layer; cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, 6–8 minutes. Reduce heat to medium; continue to cook, stirring often, until meat is just cooked through, about 1 minute more. Remove from heat. Add remaining 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; toss to combine. (Residual heat from pan will cook out any raw garlic flavor.).

Uncover couscous and fluff with a fork to separate grains. Spoon into a large shallow bowl or onto a platter. Top with steak. Cut 1 lemon into quarters and squeeze juice from 1 quarter over steak. Scatter thinly sliced cucumber and some dill sprigs on top; drizzle with oil.

Industry observers note that combine 1 cup plain whole-milk yogurt and a generous pinch of kosher salt in a small bowl; squeeze juice from 2 lemon quarters into yogurt. Stir to combine. If sauce is thick, stir in water, a spoonful at a time, to loosen.

Serve steak and couscous with yogurt sauce and remaining lemon quarter and more lemon wedges for squeezing over.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, black Friday isn't until November 27, but that hasn't stopped mattress brands from getting a head start on the holiday savings. If your current bed has seen better days or you're waking up with more aches than you went to bed with, there's no need to wait until a designated shopping day to save big on an upgrade. We've spotted the 12 best Black Friday mattress deals to explore ahead of all of your Thanksgiving festivities.

Brands like Saatva, Birch, and Beautyrest are already offering up to $1,000 off on hotel-worthy innerspring mattresses, cooling hybrids, and organic options. Whether you're a side sleeper in need of a little extra cushioning for your hips and shoulders or someone who prefers a firmer, more supportive surface, there's something worth considering before the holiday rush kicks into high gear.

Sources indicate that below, you'll find AD-tested mattresses, complete with reviewer insights, notable features, and details about the current promotions. Get ready to find your next bed without losing sleep over the price tag.

Saatva is giving shoppers who have “luxury mattress” on their Black Friday wish list a head start on savings. The brand is taking over $600 off its popular Classic queen. Designed to deliver hotel-worthy comfort at home, the innerspring mattress features a dual-coil construction; a plush, three-inch Euro pillow top; and targeted lumbar support that helps promote spinal alignment. It also comes in three firmness options—plush soft, luxury firm, and firm—making it a versatile choice for different sleep positions. Reviewer Erin Kaplan, a combination side-and-stomach sleeper, praises the mattress's supportive feel, durability, and temperature regulation. “Overall, I get a better night’s sleep on a more consistent basis since I switched mattresses,” she says. Complimentary white-glove delivery, a 365-night sleep trial, and a lifetime warranty round out the perks of this high-end buy.

It has been revealed that another name brand with an impressive 180 years of history, Stearns & Foster has a reputation for hotel-quality bedding you’ll find in luxury hotel chains like the Ritz-Carlton. They’ve already kicked off their Black Friday sale, which promises up to $1,000 off select adjustable mattress sets and a $300 Visa gift card with all mattress purchases. Senior visuals editor Melissa Maria raves about her Stearns & Foster Lux Estate Mattress, noting its seamless white glove delivery service was a game-changer. The level of firmness required an adjustment period for her, but the Tempur-Indulge memory foam layer and added pillow top gave it a more plush feel. “I’m a very light and finicky sleeper and it always takes me time to adjust to any sort of change, but my husband remarked at how well he slept and how much better his back felt after the first couple of nights sleeping on this mattress,” she says.

It has been revealed that beautyrest’s long-lasting mattresses are powered with advanced pocketed coil technology, helping couples with motion isolation and providing zoned support. The brand’s Black Friday sale is underway, and you can now save up to $1,000 on select mattress and adjustable base sets. Audience development manager Emma Tubbs recommends the Beautyrest Black Series One Mattress, which she indicates has the “perfect firmness.” “As someone who continuously changes positions throughout the night, the quilted innerspring construction nicely accommodated my tossing and turning,” she writes in her review. “I often fall asleep on my stomach and move to my side and even my back as I fall deeper into REM—I feel supported by this mattress in each position.” Plus, the motion isolation has worked well for her, as she continues sleeping through her husband’s 5:30 a.m. wakeups.

Over the past century, Serta’s become known for making comfortable, solidly priced mattresses. As it stands, the brand is offering the lowest price we’ve seen in months on the Serta Five-Star Mattress. Shopping writer Julia Harrison had this mattress-in-a-box delivered downstairs, and managed to haul it up with the help of her roommate. She refers to it as relatively lightweight (thanks to the gel-infused foam versus a heavier gel bead layer), exactly medium-firm, and made without any frills. “Nothing about it feels too hard or too soft, which I know primarily because I never think about the density or firmness of this mattress (a good sign!) and because I’ve had no back or neck problems since sleeping on it,” she says.

Selecting a firmer mattress doesn't mean you’re opting for less comfort. That’s especially true with the original PurpleFlex bed-in-a-box, presently $100 off ahead of Black Friday. Unlike traditional memory foam beds, the PurpleFlex features a two-inch GelFlex Grid designed to relieve pressure while maintaining a supportive, responsive feel. Beneath that layer, a durable foam base provides stability, making the eight-inch mattress especially appealing to back and stomach sleepers who prefer sleeping on top of their bed rather than sinking into it. AD tester Chapin Rockwell particularly likes the firm construction, reporting “less back pain and stiffness” after switching to the PurpleFlex.

In a recent development, the WinkBed is a luxury hybrid mattress that caters to your preferred sleeping style, and it’s right now 30% off as part of the brand’s Veterans Day sale. What makes the WinkBeds particularly versatile is its four firmness options: Softer, Luxury Firm, Firmer, and Plus (the last level, Plus, is designed for sleepers who need additional support). Beneath its plush yet supportive Euro pillow top, pressure-relieving gel foam and individually wrapped coils work together to provide cushioning, targeted support, and motion isolation. A moisture-wicking Tencel cover also helps promote a cooler sleeping environment. But don’t just take WinkBeds’ word for it. Contributor Mark Burka notes that the mattress "provides strong edge support and wicks away heat," two features that help distinguish it from other hybrids. Moreover, it also comes with free shipping, a 365-night sleep trial, and a lifetime warranty, offering plenty of time to determine whether it's the right fit for you.

It has been revealed that side sleepers searching for a more supportive night's rest should put shopping Nolah's early Black Friday sale at the top of their shopping list. Shopping editor Audrey Lee, who tested an earlier iteration of the Evolution, praises its high level of comfort and cooling abilities. “I found this design’s contouring quality top-tier for pressure relief, but I still had ample support thanks to the coils,” she claims. The brand is currently taking 35% off its mattresses, bringing the queen-size Evolution from $2,277 down to $1,480. Designed to cushion sensitive pressure points without sacrificing support, the luxury hybrid combines responsive AirFoam Luxe, individually wrapped coils, and targeted lumbar support to help keep the spine aligned. Shoppers can choose among Plush, Luxury Firm, and Firm options, all of which can accommodate an optional GlacioTex cooling pillow-top upgrade for additional cushioning and temperature regulation. A 365-night sleep trial, free shipping, and a limited lifetime warranty make the early holiday deal even sweeter.

To make your bedroom a little more environmentally conscious, consider starting with the Birch Natural Mattress, a medium-firm hybrid model that’s free of polyurethane foam, fiberglass, formaldehyde, and pesticides. Instead, it’s made from natural and organic materials, including breathable organic cotton, natural wool, and organic latex that’s certified by the Global Organic Latex Standard (GOLS), breathable organic cotton, and natural wool. Individually wrapped steel coils provide responsive support, while the latex offers gentle contouring (as opposed to the sinking feeling you might get from memory foam). Contributor Zoë Sessums was particularly impressed by the mattress's balance of softness and firmness, calling its feel "Goldilocks perfection." Birch Natural also features reinforced sides for additional stability that you’ll enjoy as you sit on the edge of your bed to put on your shoes. Free shipping, a 365-night sleep trial, and a limited lifetime warranty add even more appeal to the brand’s early holiday sale, which takes 25% off sitewide, bringing the queen-size Birch Natural Mattress down to $1,399 from $1,865.

Handcrafted in Illinois, this mattress combines three inches of GOLS-certified organic Dunlop latex for a breathable, responsive sleeping surface with organic cotton and wool that’s certified by the Global Organic Textile Standard (GOTS). (That’s a third party verification that ensures the organic origin and processing of the materials used in the bed.) The Natural Escape’s individually pocketed coil system features seven zones of targeted lumbar support, making the mattress a strong contender for shoppers who prefer a firmer surface. "I feel super supported," notes contributor Kristi Kellogg of her experience testing the Natural Escape. She also has zero back pain while sleeping on it and appreciates the straightforward delivery and setup process: It arrives compressed in a box and includes free shipping and returns, a 365-night sleep trial, and a 20-year warranty. Need another reason to consider making the switch? My Green Mattress is right now taking 10% off orders during its Go Green Sale, with the Natural Escape Organic Mattress queen going for $1,829, down from $2,079.

Just like the Saatva Classic Mattress, you can save up to $625 off when you buy an adjustable base or upholstered bed frame with this mattress. The luxury mattress is made with sustainable materials such as organic cotton and plant-based flame retardants. In fact, the eco-friendly construction even won over contributor Bailey Berg’s partner, an environmental scientist. It’s been four years since Berg brought the Loom & Leaf Mattress home, and she says it hasn’t lost its composure. “My partner and I joke about feeling like we’re floating on a seat of comfort,” she says. “There’s little to no sag. I think any kind of sleeper—side sleepers, stomach sleepers, and back sleepers alike—would like this supportive pick.”.

We’ve all been there: You toss and turn, flip your pillow looking for cool relief, and feel disappointed when you find nothing of the sort. If you tend to overheat easily, Casper's early Black Friday sale could be your chance to finally get a less sweaty night's sleep. Designed to keep nighttime overheating at bay, the mattress uses Casper's Snow Technology, which combines a pleasantly crisp QuickCool cover, phase-change material designed to absorb and disperse heat, and aluminum graphite HeatDelete bands that help draw excess heat away from the body. The mattress’s zoned memory foam and supportive springs also provide cushioning and spinal support without the overly plush sensation of an all-foam mattress. After testing the Snow Hybrid, contributor Kate McGregor describes its feel as "squishy when I lay down," while noting that the foam doesn't make getting out of bed difficult. She also loves its motion isolation and cooling qualities, although there were some lingering off-gassing smells after unboxing. Really, the only hot thing about this bed is its early Black Friday Deal: the sale offers over $800 off the queen-sized hybrid mattress, making now a great time to buy.

Tuft & Needle is an Arizona-based retailer touting reasonably priced mattresses made with the brand’s cooling and pressure-relieving T&N Adaptive Foam Technology. Now, the prices are even better with the pre-Black Friday sitewide sale. Everything is 20% off, including the Tuft & Needle Mint Mattress. Contributor Anna Fixsen is a side sleeper who prefers a medium-firm feel, and says she’s met her match with the Mint mattress. “I fell asleep faster and better on this mattress than my old innerspring mattress—despite being someone prone to tossing and turning—making this a great option out of all the memory foam mattresses out there,” she writes in her review. She attributes her restfulness to the invisible support layer of cushy gel beads, providing a cool, supportive slumber.

Mussels deserve your attention on weeknights. An affordable and accessible protein, they also happen to cook in less time than it takes to boil water. As the bivalves steam, they release a briny liquid, further perfuming the buttery, sake-fortified miso broth. Load up each bowl with a few good ladles, slurping every drop with an assist from crusty bread or warm rice. And why not enjoy the rest of the bottle of sake alongside your meal?

The seafood counter at your supermarket should sell rinsed and debarred mussels, but it’s easy to do at home. Discard any with cracked shells. Gently tap open raw mussels on a counter to see if they slowly close; if they do, those are okay to use. Swish them in a water-filled salad spinner or colander fitted inside a bowl, draining and refilling until water runs clear (give any especially dirty ones a scrub with a sponge). Use a towel to pull off the fibrous beard and set on a towel-lined tray in the fridge until you’re ready to cook.

More seafood dinners this way: Avgolemono Seafood Stew; Spaghetti alle Vongole; and Gorgeous Green Shrimp.

Place 2 Tbsp. scallions from 8 scallions, thinly sliced on a diagonal, in a small bowl and set aside for serving.

Recent findings suggest that melt 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add 8 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining scallions to pot and cook, stirring often, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add 2 Tbsp. white miso paste and ½ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes (if using) and cook until miso is broken up and incorporated into butter, about 20 seconds. Pour in 1 cup dry sake or dry white wine and stir to combine, then add 3–3½ lb. mussels, scrubbed, debearded. Cover pot and increase heat to medium-high. Cook, shaking pot occasionally, until mussels open, 5–7 minutes (discard any that do not open). Remove pot from heat.

Sources indicate that squeeze 1 lemon half over mussels. Cut remaining 1 lemon half into wedges for serving. Taste broth and season with kosher salt if needed.

It has been revealed that ladle mussels and broth among shallow bowls, then scatter reserved scallions over. Serve with country-style bread or steamed white rice if desired and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“Bono is usually a man with a lot of ideas,” indicates photographer/director Anton Corbijn, “so initially we have a conversation and then maybe I make it more theatrical or whatever.”.

That overly casual-sounding process has led to the most extensive collaboration ever between a band and a visual artist. Since their first encounter in 1982, Corbijn has helped establish the evolving public image of U2 across album covers, music videos, and photo shoots for almost 45 years, including the landmark cover of The Joshua Tree, the all-out aesthetic reboot for Achtung Baby, and music videos including “Pride (In the Name of Love)” and “One.” (The partnership is extensively documented in Corbijn’s 2005 book U2&i.) Most recently, they reconnected for a connected pair of surreal and evocative videos—“The Greatest Show on Earth” and “Can’t Stop Us Now”—from U2’s latest album Carnaval de Luz, the band’s first full-length release in nine years.

It has been revealed that bono recalls first noticing Corbijn’s work when he was still a teenager, especially a photo of Joy Division that ran on the cover of NME in 1980 following the suicide of lead singer Ian Curtis. “Seeing Anton make these images of these people, they were actual human beings,” he notes. “We think from their music that they’re certainly not, but then these images prove that they’re people who lived just across the way. It’s like making movies.”.

Indeed, Corbijn has gone on to direct films, including the acclaimed 2007 Ian Curtis biopic Control, as well as doing videos and album covers for Nirvana, Tom Waits, Metallica, the Rolling Stones, and R.E.M. and decades of ongoing work with Depeche Mode.

“It’s difficult for a photographer to shoot bands,” he says, “because bands have an identity, and you need to somehow get that right. It’s very important that the pictures I do with Depeche Mode don’t look like the pictures I do with U2.”.

Recently, Bono (in Fresh York City) and Corbijn (in Amsterdam) met up on Zoom to discuss their unprecedented alliance, playfully referring to each other as “A” and “B” and recalling shared moments and mutual inspiration. (They also revealed that Corbijn made a film about the American leg of the 2017 Joshua Tree 30th-anniversary tour, which they are planning to bring to local screens during next year’s Carnaval de Luz: The Greatest Show on Earth dates.).

“There are, of course, many occasions where a great artist springs up on their own—a painter, a songwriter, a photographer, a filmmaker, novelist,” claims Bono. “But often there’s some kind of community. U2’s music certainly comes out of community, and Anton is a huge part of our community.”.

This conversation was edited for length and clarity.

Industry observers note that bono: The great stories in songwriting are often unexplained, not resolved. And Anton, your gift to U2 was that you want the emotions to cohere rather than to explain the music. If everything adds up, it adds up to nothing. It’s the thing that you can’t explain that keeps you going back to the work—which sounds like that might be an excuse for laziness, for half-finished lyrics, but I felt over our time together that you finished some of the lyrics for me with your images.

In a recent development, the comedy and the tragedy of “The Greatest Show on Earth” is a real example of that. I hope it’s not too close to the bone with the singer playing the leader of a religious cult and the women doing all the work. But look, anyone who can get the members of U2 to put on beards and look like ZZ Top is some sort of shaman. To do one of your film clips is to risk being very silly—and whilst I don’t have that fear in general, as is obvious from the pratfalls I’ve made in my life and artistic life, the other three members of the band do have a certain amount of self-respect, and so only their faith in you as an artist and trust in you as a friend would have them participate at the level they did.

Recent findings suggest that anton Corbijn: I don’t want to make anybody look silly, but weird is good, and strange, and like you noted. I have a very intuitive approach, and we collaborate. Famously, what became the cover of The Joshua Tree was me looking at the desert for a photograph for an album U2 were calling Desert Songs.

Industry observers note that bono: Yeah, yeah, that’s right. Another [potential] title was The Two Americas. But wasn’t it on that shoot we found the title? Via you, and especially the way you pronounced “Yah-shua Tree.” I hope you still find it amusing that we find your Dutch accent amusing.

Recent findings suggest that but as often happens in art, the reason becomes clear years later. That’s the strangest thing—it didn’t start with the Joshua tree; it’s at the end you discovered it. On Carnaval de Luz, we knew from the beginning what we were thinking about, but we discovered it at the very end with the image maker, with the icon maker.

Recent findings suggest that corbijn: I remember we had a three-day shoot, and we were driving from Reno to Palm Springs, and after the first day, we walked together to the hotel in the desert. And I told you about this tree that I liked so much. I had this landscape camera where the lens moved, so you could get very long shots. I thought it was really nice that you have a tree on the front, and the image goes on to the back, and the band is on the back. So I was talking about that, and I mentioned the name of that tree. And then, the next morning, you came down with the Bible in your hand and said, “It’s got to be The Joshua Tree!”.

Bono: We had no idea that Joshua is the same name as Jesus, Yeshua, and what post-punk band would put an album out called The Jesus Tree? But we forget, because the world is going through some parched times presently, that even though the ’80s seemed to be great for a lot of people—you had the Material Girl and dance music, and New York was flying—there was something up in the ’80s. Springsteen would say there was a darkness on the edge of town. And I think for us to dress as pilgrims, as Irish people coming to America, was absurd but actually very effective.

It has been revealed that we were trying to figure out, How do you not look stupid on a magazine cover? How are you to be? I mean, we were in our early 20s, and we were not elegantly wasted, as was kind of the mood of the time—if you’re in a rock ’n’ roll band, you should have the good manners to at least look like you’re about to die any minute. You don’t want to look earnest. And we needed to find our own way of, How do we be ourselves? What masks can we choose to reveal ourselves? What is the iconography of whatever the project is? That naturally led on to Zoo TV and all the various shoots we did for Achtung Baby and Zooropa and all that.

According to recent reports, my favorite session of ours, Anton, is when we shot for Pop in Miami. They’re some of my favorite photographs of the band because you seem to photograph what the work is rather than what the people are. So for Pop, you went for bright colors and mischief and charm. Anton, do you remember those sessions in Miami?

Sources indicate that corbijn: Yeah, vividly actually, because you were still recording at the time, in the basement in a hotel. We were young and playful, and so many different options with clothing as well. And we tried funny-looking shots and playful shots, serious stuff as well, but I think after The Joshua Tree, I was attempting to bring more life into the pictures with color use. I also remember you saying that at the time that you liked the colorful stuff I did with Depeche. It was not new for me, but we did cross-processing so the color became very vivid, and that’s why Achtung Baby looks so colorful.

Recent findings suggest that bono: We always live by this sort of modus that the songs will tell us what to do. The songs will tell us how to look, how to behave, what the live show is about, how to dress onstage and sometimes even offstage—and because your thing was, “I’m shooting the song; I’m shooting the material, not you,” I think that really worked for us.

Recent findings suggest that one thing I’d like to ask you, Anton: Would you be comfortable talking about the religiosity of your work? It’s a recurring theme for you, and can you explain a little bit of that?

In a recent development, corbijn: Not really, actually. I don’t go to church anymore. My father was a pastor, and my grandfather, and all my uncles, and so it sort of made me walk away from it. But I think because I grew up with it, it’s just in my visual language. We grew up next to a cemetery, and maybe that had something to do with it, but the visual iconography, the Christian iconography, is in our society so much that it’s hard to not use it. Sometimes it’s just there—like the first pictures I did with Depeche Mode in ’81, when they were a teeny-tiny pop band, was in this studio in London, and there was this cross with Jesus on it in the garden. So in the photograph, they were like teenybop guys, but still Christ is hanging in the picture.

According to recent reports, bono: Religion has often been such a negative force in the world. It’s very understandable that we would try to avoid the obvious imagery associated with it, but in my life it’s turned into a very positive thing. It’s sort of buoyed me up. But you have it in all your work, despite your attempt to get away from it, I suppose.

Corbijn: I was just thinking, in the “One” video, there’s the Father, Son, and the Holy Ghost, and the band, and the woman. It was all in there. I think it’s very nice that I knew your father and you met my father.

It has been revealed that bono: Yes, that’s right. Two powerful men in our lives. But again, your ability to talk people into doing things—you asked my father to stand on a seesaw, and he went along with it, he was fascinated by it. And then you got the four fathers of U2, the fathers and sons.

In a recent development, corbijn: That was one of my favorite pictures of U2. There’s a lot of depth in it.

Bono: What other favorites do you have, Anton?

Recent findings suggest that corbijn: Well, I made a book of 500 pages on U2, full of pictures I like. I like some of the photographs we did around Rattle and Hum. That was not a good time for me, but I think there’s some good pictures there. Also on the rooftop in L.A.—I don’t mean the playing one, but the one when we looked at the rooftop, when we discovered it.

In a recent development, bono: I found this hotel, a real hotel called the Rosslyn Million Dollar Hotel. I was reading Bukowski at the time, listening to Tom Waits, and I walked into this hotel. I couldn’t believe it existed. Eventually I managed to convince Wim Wenders to make a film there. And we so loved the sign, the Million Dollar Hotel, that when we played on that rooftop, we rebuilt the sign.

It has been revealed that corbijn: Yeah but on a much smaller rooftop. I’m in the video, actually. I’m trying to get through the crowd, pointing to the policeman that I have a pass, and he goes, “You go that way!”.

Bono: That poor man, that policeman who pulled the plug. By all accounts, his children tortured him, and he was the most unpopular cop in Los Angeles. He was just doing his job.

Let me see if I one more question for my hero and friend...

Corbijn: I have a question. Why?

According to recent reports, no further questions: All’s Fair season 2 is one of the most fashionable series you can stream right now. When the show debuted just over a year ago, it made headlines for being Hulu’s biggest scripted launch in three years. Is it any wonder?
